learning_outcomes.text: Provide the basic knowledge, methods, and tools useful for the correct definition of mechanical design activities.
Reproduce the representation of a simple mechanical system.
Define the relationship between the elements of a mechanical system.
Calculate the constraints of a mechanical system.
Draw the stress diagrams of components.
Compute the maximum tensile state of components.
Verify the fatigue life of simple mechanical components.
Calculate the strength of some basic bolted and welded structures.
Select the most appropriate rolling bearings to be positioned as constraints of shafts, pins, and axes.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the study and to the analysis of a mechanical system
Function analysis of a product
The kinematics and dynamic representation of a simple mechanical system and the relationships between the machine elements
The rigid body equilibrium
Work and power
Motion and energy transmission between the machine elements
Morphologic characteristics and the load analysis of the mechanical systems
Structural models and tensile state analysis
Stress concentration factors
Residual stresses
The normal stress
The bending stress
The shear stress
The torsion stress
The failure of materials under static loads
The equivalent uniaxial stress in case of static load
The dynamic failure of the metals
The fatigue stress
The S-N (Wlöer) curves and the Haigh diagrams
The surface, gradient, dimension and load effects on the fatigue strength
The equivalent uniaxial stress in case of dynamic load
The medium stress effects on the fatigue strength
The gear design
The loads applied by the gears on the shafts
Fundamentals of bolted and welded structures: the static calculation and verification
The rolling bearings selection and their life prediction
assessment_rules: The assessment consists of a written test and an oral test. The written test, lasting three hours, involves solving three numerical exercises: resolution of an isostatic structure, selection/verification of a connection (bolted, welded, or roller bearing), and fatigue verification of a notched structure. Each exercise is worth a maximum of 10 points. To pass the written test, students must achieve at least 6 points on the first exercise and an overall grade of at least 18/30. The oral exam verifies theoretical knowledge and must be completed within the three sessions of the exam period in which the written exam was taken. The grade obtained in the written test can be refused only once.
